statement: You are given an m × n board in which every cell is 'X' or 'O'. In this visualizer the board is entered as numbers: 0 for 'X' and 1 for 'O'.

A region is a group of 'O' cells connected through shared edges (up, down, left or right). A region is surrounded when none of its cells lies on the border of the board, so it is closed in by 'X' cells on every side.
Capture every surrounded region by turning all of its 'O' cells into 'X'. Regions that reach the border stay as they are. The board is changed in place; return the board after the captures.

examples.explanation: The three 'O's in the middle form one region with no border cell, so all three are captured. The 'O' on the bottom row lies on the border and survives.
The two 'O's in the left column touch the border and stay. The pair in column 2 never reaches the border, so both are captured.
Every 'O' sits on the border, so there is nothing to capture and the board is unchanged.
